title: 5 signals your brand is invisible to AI search
target_audience: B2B service business owners — agencies, consultants, MSPs
key_points: AI search tools can't find you by problem type, only by name
Your last published content is more than 3 months old
You rank for your own name but not for the problems you solve
No independent sources mention you in context of your expertise
Clients can't describe what you do without seeing your website first

title: The Presence Debt Calculator: how much visibility have you lost this quarter
target_audience: B2B service business owners who know they've been quiet but don't know how to quantify it
key_points: Presence Debt = missed contact points × time elapsed × audience memory decay
Score 5 dimensions: publishing frequency, channel consistency, search footprint, referral mentions, client recognition
Each week of silence costs more than the previous week — the decay is non-linear
Debt is easier to prevent than repay — the framework shows why

title: The exact LinkedIn post structure that gets saved, not just liked
target_audience: B2B service business owners who post on LinkedIn but get engagement without leads
key_points: Saves happen when the post answers a question the reader will face again
Structure: problem recognition → mechanism → reframe → one actionable sentence
The hook must name the reader's situation, not the writer's expertise
End with a question that makes the reader think, not a prompt to engage

title: How AI search decides who to recommend — and what it ignores
target_audience: B2B service business owners curious about AI search but not sure what to do about it
key_points: Myth: AI recommends whoever has the best website. Reality: AI surfaces whoever appears most consistently in context
Myth: SEO for AI is different from regular SEO. Reality: it's consistency of authoritative signal over time
Myth: you need to optimize for AI. Reality: you need to be present where AI looks — not game the algorithm
The right model: think about what a well-read colleague would say about your firm, then ask if that evidence exists online

title: Presence audit: is your brand findable between client conversations
target_audience: B2B service businesses whose clients come mostly from referrals and want to understand their passive visibility
key_points: Can a warm referral find you without asking for your website?
Does your content appear when someone searches the problem you solve?
Would a buyer who heard your name once be able to verify your expertise independently?
Is your most recent public content less than 60 days old?
Do two or more independent sources mention you in a relevant professional context?
Can someone understand your positioning in under 30 seconds on any platform?

title: How to introduce your expertise so AI search can categorize it
target_audience: B2B service business owners writing their About page, LinkedIn summary, or content bio
key_points: AI search needs category signals, not personality statements
Structure: [problem you solve] + [who has it] + [how you solve it differently] — in that order
Avoid: 'passionate about helping businesses grow' — no category signal
Use: 'I work with [type of business] who struggle with [specific problem] by [specific approach]'
Repeat the category signal across all public touchpoints — not just one page

title: The Compound Presence model: why consistent beats brilliant
target_audience: B2B service business owners who know they should publish more but can't justify the time if one post doesn't get results
key_points: Each piece of content has two jobs: the immediate engagement AND the permanent presence signal
Compound Presence means each post makes the next post work harder — not independent bets
The minimum viable frequency for compound effect is 2x/week on at least one channel
Visibility that accumulates is worth more than visibility that spikes — the math on why
Three conditions for compound effect: consistent voice, consistent topic, consistent contact point

title: 3 things your ideal client checks about you before the first conversation
target_audience: B2B service business owners preparing for a sales conversation or wondering why warm leads go cold
key_points: Recent content: is there evidence you're active and current in your field?
Social proof without asking: do others reference you, not just review you?
Consistency of voice: does the person they'll meet match the person they found online?
